The feet are the foundation. the connection to the ground. from there, all begins. Most of us don’t think about our feet until something hurts… a stiff ankle, a wobble, a balance that isn’t what it used to be. It doesnt´end there. Iliosacral pain, tight pelvic floor from dysbalance of intrinsic and extrinsic muscles. The feeling of instability, ungroundedness.  It´s never just one area in the body, but we can start supporting that area and move up into the other areas, that help regulating our body on deeper levels.  Not just in physcial stability but nerve supply, fluid and pressure regulations... and I am talking about the 7 diaphragms. The foot arches as horizontal layers are on of them these 3 stretches on a block wake up the arches, soften the ankles, bring strength back into muscles we rarely think to use. small movements… steady ground… a body that knows how to hold itself up. just a block. a few minutes. bare feet remembering what they can do. start before you need to. that’s the whole practice🧡 Save this for your next practice and send it to someone who needs this.  #osteopath #foundation #feet

The key to a strong and stable structure lies beneath the surface. Let’s dig into the fascinating world of footings! 🔍 🌐 Footing Fundamentals: Footing is the unsung hero of construction, responsible for transferring the weight of a building to the solid ground below. It’s a game-changer! But how do you choose the right type of footing? 🤔 ✅ Factors to Consider: 1️⃣ Depth of Safe-Bearing Strata 2️⃣ Soil Type & Condition 3️⃣ Superstructure’s Needs 🏠 Isolated Footing: When you’ve got single columns standing solo, isolated footings are your go-to choice. These footings ensure stability, prevent sinking, and keep things safe and sound. 💰 Cost-Effective Choice: Isolated footings are often the budget-friendly option, especially when the ground’s properties remain consistent. Now, let’s talk types of isolated footings: 1️⃣ Pad Footing: Versatile in shape, efficient, but watch out for lateral forces! What’s your preference – circular, rectangular, or square? 2️⃣ Sloped Footing: Less concrete, less reinforcement, and a sleek 45-degree slope. It’s all about maintaining that perfect angle! 📐 3️⃣ Stepped Footing: A classic approach for residential buildings, although it’s become less common in recent years. 🏘️ 4️⃣ Combined Footing: When space is tight, and individual footings won’t cut it, we combine forces! 💪 What’s your experience with footings? I know people like this mean well and are trying to help but photos don’t always tell the whole story and advice like this can end up harming the horse it’s recommended for. with the deformity Gus has in this limb & his pigeon toed stance, taking that lateral heel down is something many have done & done to his detriment. I get it. everyone is taught what a good hoof is supposed to look like and how to trim a hoof to fit that ideal. an “ideal” cookie cutter trim can be the exact opposite of ideal on a hoof with distortion above it. Gus would walk away from those trims, immediately buckle in his knee and struggle to be able to lock it. it would take me years to understand why. Gus has some beautiful symmetrical feet and then he has this one. for years he had been trimmed symmetrically and we believe that is what caused not only the twisting/distortion of the hoof capsule but exacerbated the arthritic changes in his knee. “just trying to do the right thing and make a healthy looking foot” was not the right thing for this specific foot. always lead with asking questions if you’re looking to give advice. “have you tried this? are his heels as imbalanced as they appear to be?” maybe there is more to the story and you do have some really helpful advice to offer with more information but if I didn’t know any better, I probably would have seen this markup and thought “holy crap, maybe that *is* super imbalanced and I need to bring that heel down quite a bit” and wound up causing further issues. I think we are on the right track with this hoof/limb currently but time will tell. #hoofcare #opticalillusion #learnontiktok #horsetok #horsecare
